title: Beyond Actions: Learning Future Operation Targets for Vision-Language-Action Models
authors: Min Lin, Bokai Zhou, Jianqi Lin, Kaiyuan Yang, Yicheng Chang, Junjie Yu, Xiaofan Liu, Jianhua Han, Rui Li, Shen Zhao, Xiaodan Liang

tldr.zh: AFCE 将示范动作、实际机器人运动和未来视觉变化联合编码为可解码的 Effect 监督目标，训练 π₀.₅ 根据当前观测预测 Effect，再解码为臂手动作，从而将动作及其执行结果共同纳入 VLA 策略学习。
tldr.en: AFCE jointly encodes demonstrated actions, realized robot motion and future visual transitions into action-decodable Effect targets, trains π₀.₅ to predict Effects from current observations, and decodes them into arm–hand commands, incorporating actions and their realized consequences into VLA policy learning.

evaluation_scope.zh: 第一阶段融合动作、手掌／指尖／关节实际变化与稀疏视觉变化，以三类重建监督学习时序 Effect；随后冻结编码器并缓存标签。第二阶段将 π₀.₅ 的预测接口改为 Effect 空间，以流匹配、解码动作误差和相邻手指动作差分共同训练策略及状态条件解码器。部署只用当前图像、指令和本体状态，预测 Effect 并解码动作块，执行前缀后重新观测；未来证据编码器不上线。单／双臂共享 Effect 主干，保留配置专用接口，不代表已验证跨手不变性。DexJoCo 仿真使用 Panda＋Allegro，6 项单臂＋5 项双臂任务、共 1,100 条示范；rand-obj 下每任务每环境种子 50 次、3 种子，共 1,650 次。总体成功率 50.97%（π₀.₅ 为 39.15%）；双臂 37.33% 对 9.73%，单臂 62.33% 对 63.67%，精细控制仍有退步。每方法一个训练检查点，统计反映环境种子变化，未报告真机策略验证。
evaluation_scope.en: Stage I fuses actions, realized palm/fingertip/joint changes and sparse visual transitions with three reconstruction objectives, then freezes the tokenizer and caches temporal Effect targets. Stage II adapts π₀.₅ to Effect-space flow matching and jointly trains the policy and state-conditioned decoder with decoded-action and adjacent-finger-difference losses. Deployment uses current images, instruction and proprioception, decodes predicted Effects, executes a prefix and observes again; future-evidence encoders remain offline. Single/dual-arm configurations share an Effect backbone with separate interfaces, without established cross-hand invariance. DexJoCo simulation uses Panda + Allegro: six single-arm and five bimanual tasks, 1,100 demonstrations; rand-obj evaluation uses 50 trials per task per environment seed across three seeds, totaling 1,650. Overall success is 50.97% versus π₀.₅'s 39.15%; bimanual means are 37.33%/9.73%, single-arm 62.33%/63.67%, with precision regressions. One trained checkpoint per method means variation is across environment seeds; hardware policy validation is not reported.
